newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Frankfurt, Paris roar ahead, London lags.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Frankfurt, Paris roar ahead, London lags.

text.p: Frankfurt and Paris stocks powered ahead on Wednesday encouraged by another record close overnight on Wall Street but London was in the doldrums, hit by worries over higher interest rates.

On currency markets, the dollar strengthened slightly against the yen, shrugging off a sharp rise in Japan's current account surplus, and climbed to 41-month highs against the German currency, at 1.7625 marks.

Frankfurt was the best performer in early trade, climbing over one percent to a trading high of 4,056.83 points on the blue-chip DAX index, propelled by the stronger dollar and record-breaking run on Wall Street.

"There seems to be nothing around to brake us at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader. "The dollar is giving us a push, Bunds (government bonds) are helping, the U.S. is helping and there are no negative corporate stories out there. I don't see any justification for pulling out, even at these highs."

Among the strong climbers was retailer Metro, already in favour after saying it might buy a Dutch cash-and-carry firm, which put on 8.6 marks to 225 in early trade. Several German research houses had recommended the stock.
The Paris bourse made early gains of 1.35 percent , with investors taking heart from Wall Street and the dollar , which boosts prospects for French exporting businesses as it strengthens.

The engine behind much of the bull run in Europe was New York's recent strength. Wall Street rose more than 100 points on the Dow Jones industrial average to close at a peak of 7,962.31 points on Tuesday.

It was the 30th record this year for the world's most widely watched stock index, whose previous record of 7,895.81 came only last week, and investors expressed confidence about the outlook for the U.S. economy and second-quarter earnings.

"Eight thousand is a foregone conclusion at this point," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd in New York. "We've been hemming and hawing just below 8,000, and the next time we make a move we'll probably blast right through."
But London was largely unmoved, preoccupied by its concerns with a two-day Bank of England meeting on interest rates due to start on Wednesday and the market expecting a decision on Thursday.
The blue-chip FTSE index started trade down about 0.5 percent but managed to claw back the early losses to edge into positive ground by mid-morning.
Many analysts were predicting an increase of at least 25 basis points to curb inflationary pressures.

"The arguments over whether it is going to be 25 or 50 basis points are really semantics. Twenty five is adequate for now and everyone knows there is going to be more. Fifty looks like an indictment of the (new Labour government's first) budget," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson strategist Philip Isherwood.

"We're not going to see many people wanting to buy on a day like today, with that sort of thing hanging in the balance, and although they'll probably try to push the market higher we won't see that lasting," said another dealer.

In currencies, the dollar climbed to a 3-1/2 year high against the mark at 1.7625 marks, with the Germany currency hurt by a subdued economic outlook for the country after Bonn reported a rise of 11,000 in unemplyment for June.
The dollar also climbed by half a yen to 113.06 yen despite a big increase in Japan's May current account surplus.

Although the current account was within expectations and the impact on the dollar limited, analysts said it remains a big political issue and is likely to keep a lid on dollar gains against the yen for the foreseeable future.

"Such a rise would of no consequence if it were not for protectionists in Washington, but political dynamics always dominate while economic ones often do not," said Ken Landon, economist at Deutsche Morgan
Sterling remained at six-year highs against the German currency, at 2.97 marks, supported by speculation of an immiment increase in interest rates coming out of the Bank of England meeting.
CURRENCIES AT 0945 GMT
The dollar was at 112.95 yen and 1.7627 marks compared to 112.57 and 1.7594 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.6 points at 4,761.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 56.12 points at 4,062.52.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 37.10 points at 2,966.91.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $315.75 per ounce, compared to Tuesday's close of $321.95. Silver was at $4.27, down nine cents.
